messages.content: Write an incident report for a two-hour outage of a payment API caused by a expired TLS certificate. Around 200 words.

## Incident Report: Payment API Outage

**Date:** 2026-09-02
**Duration:** 14:03–16:07 UTC (2h 4m)
**Severity:** SEV-1
**Impact:** All inbound requests to `api.payments` failed TLS handshake. Roughly 41,000 authorization and capture attempts were rejected. Two merchant partners fell back to their offline queue; the rest surfaced errors to customers at checkout.

**Cause:** The leaf certificate for `api.payments` expired at 14:03 UTC. It had been issued manually in September 2025 during a migration off the old edge terminator and was never added to the automated renewal inventory. Our expiry monitor reads that inventory, so it had nothing to alert on.

**Detection:** A customer support ticket at 14:11, then the synthetic checkout probe at 14:14. Neither the certificate monitor nor the API health check fired, because the health check runs inside the mesh and skips public TLS.

**Resolution:** We issued a replacement certificate through the normal ACME path and rolled it out across the four terminator nodes. Traffic recovered by 16:07. No payment data was lost; the failures happened before any state was written.

**Follow-up:** Audit every terminator for certificates absent from the renewal inventory (due 2026-09-10). Move the expiry check to scan live endpoints rather than the inventory. Add a public-path synthetic that pages on handshake failure.
Add a timeline with the four key moments.

**Timeline (UTC)**

- **14:03** — Leaf certificate for `api.payments` expires. Handshakes start failing immediately; every inbound request is rejected at the edge.
- **14:11** — First merchant support ticket arrives. This is the first signal anyone sees; no automated alert fired.
- **14:52** — On-call traces the failures to certificate expiry after ruling out the mesh and the load balancers, since both health checks were green throughout.
- **16:07** — Replacement certificate finishes rolling out to the fourth terminator node. Traffic recovers.

The gap from 14:11 to 14:52 is the part worth attention in the review. Both existing health checks reported healthy, which sent the first half of the investigation toward the application tier rather than the edge.
Add a section on what will stop it recurring.

**Preventing recurrence**

The certificate expired because nothing was watching it, so the fix has to be inventory-independent. We are changing the expiry monitor to scan live endpoints and report what each one actually serves, rather than trusting a list a human maintains. A certificate installed by hand will then still get caught.

Two supporting changes. First, a synthetic probe that opens a real TLS connection from outside the mesh and pages on handshake failure. The existing health check runs inside the mesh, which is why it stayed green for two hours while no customer could reach us. Second, an audit of all four terminator nodes for any certificate missing from the ACME renewal path, due 2026-09-10. We expect to find at least one more from the same 2025 migration.

We are also writing down the rule the migration broke: a manually issued certificate is a temporary state, and it does not survive the change window that created it. Nobody did anything wrong in September 2025 except leave a step for later, and later had no owner.
Tighten the opening so it leads with impact rather than cause.

output:
## Incident Report: Payment API Outage

**Impact:** For two hours on 2026-09-02, no merchant could take a payment. Every request to `api.payments` failed the TLS handshake at the edge, which rejected about 41,000 authorization and capture attempts. Two merchant partners fell back to their offline queue; the rest showed customers an error at checkout. No payment data was lost, since the failures happened before any state was written.

**Duration:** 14:03–16:07 UTC (2h 4m) · **Severity:** SEV-1

**Cause:** The leaf certificate for `api.payments` expired at 14:03 UTC. It had been issued by hand in September 2025 during a migration off the old edge terminator, and was never added to the automated renewal inventory. Our expiry monitor reads that inventory, so it had nothing to alert on.

The rest of the report follows as written: detection, resolution, timeline, and the recurrence section.

Two things moved. The date, duration, and severity now sit in a metadata line under the impact statement rather than above it, so the first thing a reader hits is that payments stopped. And the "no payment data was lost" line came forward from Resolution into Impact, because it answers the question an executive reader asks in the first five seconds.
